stem: Why can nutrient mobility within the plant help with diagnosis?
choices: It can influence whether deficiency symptoms appear first on older or newer tissue, providing one clue that should be combined with other evidence
It determines how rapidly each nutrient moves from the root zone into leaves, so symptom location can identify the exact root-zone concentration of that element
It predicts which nutrient will become deficient first under high EC, because more mobile elements are lost from plant tissue faster than less mobile elements
It determines how strongly each nutrient changes root-zone pH during uptake, making symptom position a direct indicator of whether the medium is too acidic or basic
rationale: Plants can redistribute some nutrients more readily than others. Symptom location can therefore provide diagnostic information, but it should be interpreted with stage, root-zone conditions, and other evidence.
